Return to the live edge when sending a chat message (#1384)

Bug #287: an outbound message vanished after send while "Jump to latest"
appeared even though the thread was already at the bottom. A refresh restored
both.

Root cause is one flag. The optimistic event is dispatched through
receiveRealtimeEvent, which only writes the render cache when
timelineUi.autoScrollPinned is true; otherwise the event is diverted to an
invisible pending buffer and hasUnseenActivity is set. The sender therefore
never saw their own message, and that same flag is what lights the jump control,
whose visibility expression ORs hasUnseenActivity with isNearBottom so being at
the bottom cannot suppress it.

The two flags disagree by construction: any upward wheel tick unpins with no
distance threshold, while "at the bottom" allows 96px of slack, and re-pinning
requires an explicit downward scroll event. Nudging the wheel up and then typing
leaves the viewport at the live edge with the session marked as not following.

Sending is an explicit move to the live edge, so pin before inserting the
optimistic event. That renders the sender's message, flushes the buffered
events, and clears hasUnseenActivity, which puts the jump control back in sync.

Deliberately narrow: an earlier attempt also made suspendAutoFollow ignore
upward scrolls inside the live-edge threshold, which broke the existing
guarantee that a user can escape auto-follow while the agent is streaming. That
half was dropped rather than weakened.

The existing optimistic-send test asserted the message landing in the pending
buffer while unpinned, which is the defect this fixes; it now observes the
optimistic event in the timeline cache instead.

* Settle a sent message by its own id instead of guessing (#48)

arrives on its own. Only settle when the response actually carries a message

* Live-stream web replies with interpolated reveal and flash-free handoff (#510)

Telemetry on prod-equivalent code showed the reply pipeline delivering
deltas the UI never painted: providers often burst the whole tool-call body
at the end, the slot gate (hasStreamingContent && isStreaming) hid the card
the instant done arrived, and the outbound message event nulled the stream
one commit before the timeline painted the message — no visible streaming,
then a blank flash, then the full reply.

Now: the typewriter reveal runs for every arrival pattern (incremental or
burst), decoupling visual cadence from network cadence, and accelerates 4x
once the stream finishes; the slot survives done until handoff; the
persisted message is suppressed in the timeline while the card owns the
content, and the swap happens in a single reducer commit once the reveal
catches up (10s safety valve if the send never persisted). Markdown cost is
bounded by block-level memoization — completed blocks are stable strings
that never re-parse, only the tail block re-commits at 7Hz with unclosed
code fences repaired, and the sub-commit tail renders as a plain span.
Backend: the first content delta flushes immediately instead of waiting out
the batching window.
